summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission following allogeneic stem cell transplant and severe chronic graft-versus-host disease was admitted for malaise after recently discontinuing oxycodone. He had no signs of active infection, with negative blood and urine cultures, and stable chest imaging showing only mild residual opacities. His symptoms improved significantly upon restarting oxycodone, supporting a diagnosis of mild opioid withdrawal. Liver enzymes were mildly elevated, likely due to medication effects, and thyroid function showed a low TSH with normal free T4, prompting no change in levothyroxine dose. His chronic conditions, including sclerodermatous GVHD, lower extremity wounds, and tachycardia, were managed supportively. He was discharged home on a tapering oxycodone regimen with plans to monitor liver function and follow up with specialty care.
